# Application holdout on DaCapo

This follow-up was specified after the eight-library study and its two local exploratory baselines. Freeze this file in Git before collecting DaCapo counts. The test set is the DaCapo 9.12-MR1-bach release. It provides independent workloads, application code and output validation in a single versioned distribution. This is a transfer test on a legacy suite. [Official release](https://github.com/dacapobench/dacapobench/releases/tag/v9.12-MR1-bach) · [Benchmark suite paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/1167473.1167488)

## Population and traces

Use four distinct engines: Lucene indexing (luindex, lucene-core-2.4.jar, org/apache/lucene/index/), PMD Java analysis (pmd, pmd-4.2.5.jar, net/sourceforge/pmd/ast/), Xalan XSLT transformation (xalan, xalan.jar, org/apache/xalan/templates/), and Sunflow rendering (sunflow, sunflow-0.07.2.jar, org/sunflow/core/). Include subpackages, inner classes, constructors and all methods. Only original binary conditional bytecodes enter the inventory. Keep a digest of each target JAR and class. Test inputs come from DaCapo's small and default configurations, one iteration per fresh JVM, one harness thread where supported. Count the whole application process including setup in the selected packages. Run an untouched control and two instrumented repetitions per configuration. Require the harness validation to pass on each. Report any disagreement between instrumented repetitions; use the first validated repetition for scoring and retain the second for auditing. Report failures and unsupported configurations by name.

Before collecting labels, rank all eligible static sites within each application by SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string "42:" followed by the original branch ID. Take the first 96, independent of execution. Use the registered local instruction windows, prompts, checkpoint revision and frozen readouts. Compare original offsets, opcode and destinations for sampled branches against javap. Record zero-count sites and both directions, covered classes and methods. Report training/test overlap of original class hashes, method opcode hashes and near-duplicate local windows. Prune training against the pooled static test sample with the registered threshold 0.9 before fitting.

## Prediction and scoring

Train once on observed normal labels from the original eight libraries. Use their published median validation-selected hyperparameters for structural ridge, structural XGBoost, lexical ridge and the full embedding ridge. Use the lexical ridge penalty for the exploratory lexical-plus-embedding model. Fit transforms using training sites alone. The opcode baseline predicts the training median of the target opcode and falls back to the global training median. Also score the constant 0.5 and full zero-shot rating. Produce one prediction per site shared by the two configurations. Neither labels nor workload identity enter features, fitting, or model selection.

The primary comparison is full zero-shot minus lexical ridge MAE on default. The secondary incremental comparison is lexical-plus-embedding minus lexical ridge on default. Report the analogous small results and opcode-median comparator. Give each observed site equal weight within each application, and each scored application equal weight in the macro MAE. Publish per-application support and paired errors. Show the range of macro contrasts obtained by omitting each application in turn. With four selected applications, interpret direction and magnitude descriptively. Missing coverage restricts inference to the scored applications. Do not tune on these results. Report the analytic two-trace floor only on sites observed under both configurations. This experiment measures label prediction; throughput is outside scope.
